summary: A six-gate ladder that separates a vendor-reported sample announcement from allocation-grade qualification evidence. Each gate names the exact evidence required; a stance may never advance on evidence from a lower gate.

gates.name: Roadmap
gates.evidence_required: Named product and development intent in a dated vendor disclosure

gates.name: Reported sample
gates.evidence_required: Dated company sample-shipment disclosure at announcement scope only

gates.name: Customer evaluation
gates.evidence_required: Customer-named evaluation evidence attributable to the evaluated generation

gates.name: Company-reported qualification
gates.evidence_required: Named-customer qualification disclosure by the vendor

gates.name: Independently attributable qualification
gates.evidence_required: Customer-side or independently attributable qualification evidence

transfer_rules: A vendor disclosure proves the disclosure, not the underlying physical event.
Secondary press reporting cannot move a claim to verified state for an underlying event.
Certification evidence for a prior generation does not transfer to the next generation.
A dated production statement is corroborating evidence, never a substitute for qualification evidence.

questions.question: Is there a dated vendor disclosure naming the product and its development intent?
Is there a dated company disclosure of a sample shipment at announcement scope?
Is there customer-named evaluation evidence attributable to this exact product generation?
Is there a named-customer qualification disclosure from the vendor?
Is there customer-side or independently attributable qualification evidence?
Is there dated production or volume-shipment evidence?
